about: The epistola of the formulary “Saint Anne, Mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Who will find a valiant woman? Far off, and from the farthest bounds, is her price. The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will not lack spoils. She will repay him with good and not with harm every day of her life. She sought wool and flax, and worked by the counsel of her hands. She became like a merchant’s ship, bringing her bread from afar. And she rose in the night, and gave prey to her household, and provisions to her maidservants. She considered a field and bought it; from the fruit of her hands she planted a vineyard. She girded her loins with strength, and strengthened her arm. She tasted and saw that her trading is good; her lamp will not be put out in the night. She put her hand to strong things, and her fingers grasped the spindle. She opened her hand to the destitute, and stretched out her palms to the poor. She will not fear for her house from the cold of the snow, for all her household are clothed with double garments. She made herself a tapestried garment; her clothing is fine linen and purple. Her husband is renowned in the gates, when he sits with the senators of the land. She made linen cloth and sold it, and delivered a girdle to the Canaanite. Strength and beauty are her clothing, and she will laugh on the last day. She opened her mouth to wisdom, and the law of clemency is on her tongue. She watched over the paths of her house, and did not eat her bread in idleness. Her children rose up and proclaimed her most blessed; her husband too, and he praised her. Many daughters have gathered riches; you have surpassed them all. Grace is deceptive, and beauty is vain; a woman who fears the Lord, it is she who will be praised. Give her of the fruit of her hands, and may her works praise her in the gates.
